/ai/glossary/: Twenty plain-English AI terms so a non-expert can follow the rest of the /ai door without hunting definitions elsewhere.
/ai/swarms/what-an-agent-swarm-is/: A swarm is many agents on one job, and the page prices what that scale spends and what it can return.
/ai/models/typesafe/jev/: Jev returns a typed decision a program can branch on.
/ai/models/anthropic/claude-opus-5-5/: Claude Opus 5.5 is the first Claude 5.5 model, released 22 September 2026, and Anthropic prices it below Opus 5 for similar work.
/ai/models/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5/: Claude Sonnet 5.5 is the second Claude 5.5 model, released 28 September 2026, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
/ai/models/anthropic/claude-fable-5-1/: Claude Fable 5.1 is Anthropic's most capable widely released model, built for long-running agents and document work.
/ai/models/anthropic/claude-opus-5/: Claude Opus 5 is Anthropic's default model for most agentic coding and enterprise work, at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens.
/ai/models/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5/: Claude Sonnet 5 is Anthropic's faster everyday model for coding and agents, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
/ai/models/anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5/: Claude Haiku 4.5 is Anthropic's fastest near-frontier model, priced for cost-sensitive work and sub-agents.
/ai/models/openai/gpt-6-astra/: GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI's flagship for hard end-to-end work: reasoning, coding, computer use, research, and documents.
/ai/models/openai/gpt-6.1-sol/: GPT-6.1 Sol is an upgrade to GPT-6 Sol, released 29 September 2026, at $2 input, $0.10 cached input, and $10 output per million tokens.
/ai/models/openai/dots/: Dots is an always-on ChatGPT agent powered by GPT-6 Astra, with its own cloud computer and browser.
/ai/models/openai/gpt-6-sol/: GPT-6 Sol is OpenAI's mid-tier GPT-6 model for complex coding and agent work, released 22 September 2026 at $2 and $10 per million tokens.
/ai/models/openai/gpt-6-luna/: GPT-6 Luna is the cheaper, faster GPT-6 tier released with Sol on 22 September 2026, at $0.10 and $0.50 per million tokens.
/ai/models/xai/grok-4-7/: Grok 4.7 is xAI's current model for coding, agents, and knowledge work, API id grok-4.7, shipped 21 September 2026.
/ai/models/xai/models/grok-4-6/: Grok 4.6 is the prior xAI flagship and is still on the API, with a knowledge cutoff of 1 February 2026.
/ai/models/xai/models/grok-4-5/: Grok 4.5 is an xAI API model with a 500k context window.
/ai/models/xai/models/grok-4-3/: Grok 4.3 is an xAI API model with a 1 million token context window and batch pricing.
/ai/models/xai/models/grok-4-20/: Grok 4.20 is listed as three API ids, for reasoning, non-reasoning, and multi-agent use, on the same token prices as Grok 4.3.
/ai/models/xai/models/grok-build-0-1/: grok-build-0.1 is a dedicated coding model on the xAI API, separate from the Grok Build product.
/ai/models/xai/grok-build/: Grok Build is xAI's coding agent for the terminal, headless scripts, and the Agent Client Protocol.
/ai/models/xai/grok-bot/: Grok Bot is xAI's product of named bots on a cloud computer, with jobs and context that persist.
/ai/models/xai/imagine/: Imagine is xAI's image and video generation family on the API and in consumer Grok.
/ai/models/xai/voice/: Voice is xAI's spoken interface: speech to speech, speech to text, and text to speech.
/ai/models/google/gemini-flash/: Gemini 3.8 Flash is Google's current Flash model for long-horizon software work and agents at Flash speed and cost.
/ai/models/google/gemini-pro/: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview is Google's Pro-line model for harder reasoning and tool use.
/ai/models/google/gemini-flash-lite/: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite is Google's low-latency model for high-volume parsing, translation, and simple extraction.
/ai/models/google/gemma/: Gemma 4 is Google's open-weight family, separate from the hosted Gemini API.
/ai/models/meta/muse/spark/: Muse Spark is Meta's flagship multimodal model for agents, coding, and Meta AI, with 1.3 as the current developer version.
/ai/models/meta/muse/glimmer/: Muse Glimmer is Meta's 30-billion-parameter open-weight model, distilled from Muse Spark, under the Apache 2.0 license.
/ai/models/meta/muse/image/: Muse Image is Meta's image generation model, wired to Muse Spark and available on Meta AI.
/ai/models/meta/muse/video/: Muse Video is Meta's video generation model in the Muse family, still described publicly as a preview.
/ai/models/meta/muse/code/: Muse Code is Meta's terminal coding product built for Muse Spark, and it is a product surface rather than a weights release.
/ai/models/meta/llama/llama-4/: Llama 4 is Meta's current open-weight generation, centered on Scout and Maverick.
/ai/models/deepseek/flash/: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is DeepSeek's current recommended API model, id deepseek-flash, with open weights on Hugging Face.
/ai/models/deepseek/v4-pro/: DeepSeek V4 Pro remains on the API as deepseek-v4-pro after 14 September 2026, with billing unchanged until further notice.
/ai/models/deepseek/thinking/: DeepSeek thinking mode is on by default for Flash and Pro, and a caller can turn it off or change the effort.
/ai/models/deepseek/api/: DeepSeek's API speaks the OpenAI and Anthropic request shapes, and the live model ids are deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro.
/ai/models/deepseek/r1/: DeepSeek-R1 is the January 2025 open reasoner, released under an MIT license, and this page keeps it as an archive.
/ai/models/deepseek/v3/: DeepSeek-V3 was the prior chat generation, and the old deepseek-chat name is retired.
/ai/models/open-weight/mimo/: MiMo-V2.6-Pro is Xiaomi's flagship open-weight model, announced 22 September 2026 with downloadable weights.
/ai/models/open-weight/glm-5-3/: GLM-5.3 is Z.AI's flagship coding and agent model, with public weights on Hugging Face.
/ai/models/open-weight/qwen/: Qwen3.8 Max is Alibaba's lead hosted Qwen model, with an open checkpoint beside it on Hugging Face.
/ai/models/open-weight/step-5/: Step 5 Preview is StepFun's agent model on the API now, and the weights are dated 15 October 2026.
/ai/models/open-weight/kimi-k3/: Kimi K3 is Moonshot's open-weight flagship for long-horizon coding and knowledge work.
/ai/hardware/chips/terafab/: Terafab is a planned chip factory from SpaceX and Tesla in Grimes County, Texas, with a Phase 1 figure of $16.8B.
/ai/hardware/data-centers/memphis-coloss: Memphis Colossus is a hyperscale training campus. The company page lists 170 PB/s of aggregate memory bandwidth and 2.8 Tb/s per server.
/ai/models/google/gemini-4-argon/: Gemini 4 Argon was announced 30 September 2026 for trusted cyber defenders, not the public, at an intro price of $2 input and $10 output per million tokens.
/ai/what-xai-has-running/: SpaceX told investors on 12 June 2026 that Colossus and Colossus II together provide about 1 gigawatt of compute power, and the Colossus page lists 170 PB/s and 2.8 Tb/s.
/ai/hardware/chips/mtia/: MTIA 300 is in production with 216 GB HBM3E, MTIA 400 is a 72-accelerator rack, and compute FLOPS from the 300 to the 500 is 25x.
/ai/hardware/data-centers/prometheus/: Prometheus in New Albany, Ohio is over 1 gigawatt and tens of thousands of graphics chips once complete.
/ai/hardware/data-centers/hyperion/: Hyperion in Richland Parish, Louisiana is published at 5 gigawatts and more than $50 billion.
/ai/hardware/data-centers/eagle-mountain: Eagle Mountain in Utah was raised to more than $3 billion on 14 September 2026.
/ai/hardware/power/meta-nuclear/: Meta's January 2026 nuclear package is up to 6.6 gigawatts by 2035.
/ai/hardware/chips/blackwell/: GB300 NVL72 is 72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs, with 20 TB of GPU memory, 130 TB/s NVLink, and 1,440 PFLOPS of FP4 Tensor Core with sparsity.
/ai/hardware/chips/rubin/: The Rubin GPU is 50 PFLOPS of NVFP4 inference and 288 GB of HBM4, and Vera Rubin NVL72 is 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs.
/ai/hardware/chips/instinct/: The custom Instinct GPU is based on the MI450 architecture, and MI300 and MI350 are the series Meta already runs.
/ai/hardware/chips/meta/: Meta's stack is MTIA, a Broadcom 2nm accelerator through 2029, millions of Nvidia Blackwell and Rubin GPUs, and up to 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct.
